a high fat diet, particularly one rich in omega-6 fatty acids, suppresses testosterone production.
a meal rich in polyunsaturated fats or a combination of polyunsaturated and monounsaturated fats, or a meal rich in refined carbohydrates, can reduce testosterone levels.

the intake of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) significantly reduces serum testosterone production to the same degree over a 4-h period as monounsaturated fatty acids (MUFA) and PUFA combined, with refined carbohydrates (CHO) having little effect, whereas egg albumins increase testosterone levels.

the effect of different macronutrient intakes on serum testosterone concentrations.
the effect of dietary macronutrients on testosterone levels in men.
the effect of macronutrients on the testosterone levels of obese and overweight men.

a high fat diet (PUFA and MUFA) reduces testosterone levels in men.
the intake of PUFA or MUFA, or a meal of PUFA combined with refined CHO, significantly reduced testosterone levels.
a high fat meal (particularly PUFA and MU) significantly reduced serum testosterone levels, while egg albumin and CHO alone had no such effect.

a high-fat diet can reduce testosterone levels.
a low fat diet is better than a high fat diet, especially a high polyunsaturated fat diet, for men who wish to optimize their serum testosterone levels.
